result.topic_en: A theorem (§62), with proof, showing that if s equals a given continued fraction in A, B, C, ..., then bs/(a − αs) equals a related continued fraction.
result.transcription:
176
Theorema
§. 62. Si fuerit
$s = \cfrac{aA}{\alpha A + \cfrac{bB}{\beta B + \cfrac{cC}{\gamma C + \text{etc.}}}}$
erit
$\frac{bs}{a - \alpha s} = \beta A + \cfrac{cA}{\gamma B + \cfrac{dB}{\delta C + \cfrac{eC}{\varepsilon D + \text{etc.}}}}$
Demonstratio
Cum enim sit
$s = \cfrac{aA}{\alpha A + \cfrac{bB}{\beta B + \cfrac{cC}{\gamma C + \text{etc.}}}}$
si primam fractionem per A, secundam per B, tertiam per C, etc. deprimamus, prodibit
$s = \cfrac{a}{\alpha + \cfrac{b:A}{\beta + \cfrac{c:B}{\gamma + \cfrac{d:C}{\delta + \text{etc.}}}}}$
Nunc huius formae secundam fractionem supra et infra per A, tertiam per B, quartam per C multiplicemus et ita porro, et nanciscemur hanc formam:
s =

177
$s = \cfrac{a}{\alpha + \cfrac{b}{\beta A + \cfrac{cA}{\gamma B + \cfrac{dB}{\delta C + \text{etc.}}}}}$
quare si statuamus
$t = \beta A + \cfrac{cA}{\gamma B + \cfrac{dB}{\delta C + \text{etc.}}}$
erit
$s = \cfrac{a}{\alpha + \frac{b}{t}} = \frac{at}{\alpha t + b}$
vnde reperitur $t = \frac{bs}{a - \alpha s}$ q. e. d.

Euleri Op. Anal. Tom. II.    Z    ME-
